findings.claim: A dental nurse treats patients with toothache and carries out check-ups.
findings.truth: Dental nurses support dental professionals during treatment and provide oral-health advice. They do not diagnose disease or plan treatment.
findings.evidence: GDC Scope of Practice (2025), Dental nurses

findings.claim: A dental nurse explains treatment options, including risks and benefits, then invites the patient to decide.
findings.truth: A dental nurse does not diagnose disease or plan treatment; treatment options should be explained by the dentist or another appropriately qualified dental professional.
findings.evidence: GDC Scope of Practice (2025), Dental nurses

findings.claim: The definition attached to ‘individuality’ describes the right to make one’s own care decisions.
findings.truth: Individuality means recognising each service user as unique, with their own needs, preferences and life history. Choice is a separate person-centred value.

findings.claim: Autonomy is presented as a named person-centred value in the specification.
findings.truth: The named value is choice; autonomy is not one of R032’s nine listed person-centred values.

findings.claim: The specification lists eight non-verbal communication skills.
findings.truth: R032 lists seven main non-verbal items. Positioning has the sub-points space, height and personal space; the specification does not call the list an eight-item list.

findings.claim: Makaton must always be used alongside speech and cannot be used on its own.
findings.truth: Makaton is a flexible communication programme using signs, symbols and speech. Its signs and symbols can be used with speech, the written word or on their own, according to the individual’s needs.

findings.claim: Anti-bacterial sprays kill both bacteria and viruses.
findings.truth: Product effectiveness depends on the product and its instructions. A suitable disinfectant and local policy are needed where disinfection is required; not all products kill bacteria and viruses.
findings.evidence: NHS England National Standards of Healthcare Cleanliness 2025; Food Standards Agency cleaning guidance

findings.claim: Disposable gloves are needed during any direct contact with a service user’s skin.
findings.truth: Gloves are used when exposure to blood, body fluids, non-intact skin or mucous membranes is anticipated, following a risk assessment. Overuse is inappropriate.
findings.evidence: NHS England National Infection Prevention and Control Manual, standard infection control precautions

findings.claim: Overshoes are worn in operating theatres to prevent contamination being carried in.
findings.truth: Overshoes are not generally used in health and care environments. If local policy requires them, they are discarded after use.
findings.evidence: National Infection Prevention and Control Manual, footwear guidance

findings.claim: Surgical scrubs have no pockets and are always laundered at high temperatures.
findings.truth: Scrubs are clinical workwear used and laundered under local policy; they can have pockets.
findings.evidence: NHS England National Infection Prevention and Control Manual; Worcestershire Acute Hospitals theatre workwear policy

findings.claim: All hospital ward staff require surgical scrubs.
findings.truth: Clinical workwear and PPE are determined by the task, infection risk and local policy; surgical scrubs are not a universal ward requirement.
findings.evidence: NHS England National Infection Prevention and Control Manual; Northern Care Alliance workwear policy

findings.claim: A dementia residential home will use all-main-door swipe access to stop residents leaving unsupervised.
findings.truth: Access controls may be used, but restrictions on a resident require individual assessment and must be necessary, proportionate and in the person’s best interests.
findings.evidence: Care Act statutory guidance 10.67–10.68; CQC Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards guidance

findings.claim: There are three types of DBS check.
findings.truth: The specification names standard checks, enhanced checks and the barred list, but the legal DBS framework has four levels: basic, standard, enhanced, and enhanced with barred-list check. Option 1: teach the legal four levels and explain which three elements R032 names. Option 2: retain the course shorthand but call them the specification’s three DBS items, not check types.
findings.evidence: spec R032, Topic Area 4.1; DBS GOV.UK, About the Disclosure and Barring Service

summary: Checked all 13 lessons. Twelve verified surgical corrections are supplied; the DBS terminology issue needs an editorial decision because the legal framework is broader than the specification’s teaching list.
